summary: Peter Kuhlmann works in linguistics and other fields, having completed his doctoral studies under Rosemarie Lühr circa 1990–1993. He held posts at the University of Düsseldorf (~1999–2002), University of Giessen (~2002–2006), and University of Göttingen (~2006).

Peter M. Scharf is an Indologist and linguist who wrote his dissertation at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona, also studying with Shrinarayan Mishra, Ludo Rocher, and Narendranath Pandey. In 2000, he was attested in Brown University's classics department.
Peter Masefield is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under L. P. N. Perera and completed his doctorate under Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

Peter Moran specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Tufts University and completed his PhD at the University of Washington under Charles Keyes, also studying under Ngawang Nornang, Leonard van der Kuijp, and several traditional Tibetan teachers.

Peter N. Gregory is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from Harvard University in 1981 under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Smith College, Komazawa University, and the Kuroda Institute.

Peter Peterson was an Indologist who studied at the University of Edinburgh under Theodor Aufrecht and at Balliol College, Oxford. He served as a Professor at Elphinstone College (~1873–1899) and as Fellow and Registrar at the University of Mumbai (~1872–1899).

Peter Schreiner is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned degrees from Temple University, the University of Münster under Paul Hacker, and the University of Tübingen, later holding posts at Tübingen, SOAS (1988), and the University of Zurich (1990).
Peter Schwabland is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his MA at the University of Washington by 1994 under the supervision of Leonard van der Kuijp.

Peter Schwieger is a Tibetologist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Bonn, studying under Dieter Schuh. He worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and held professorships at the University of Berlin and Bonn.

Peter Skilling is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned his PhD at the EPHE and studied under Heinz Bechert. He held posts at Chulalongkorn University, EFEO, and the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation, alongside multiple visiting professorships.

Peter Stewart is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his MA, MPhil, and PhD at Clare College, Cambridge, and held posts at Cambridge, Reading, Courtauld Institute of Art, and the University of Oxford, including the Classical Art Research Centre.

Peter Zieme works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Berlin (1960–1965), he held posts at the Institut für Orientforschung, the GDR Academy of Sciences, and the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Peter van der Veer works in religious studies, Indology, and Sinology, having studied at the University of Groningen and Utrecht University. He held directorships and professorships at Utrecht, Amsterdam, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Pennsylvania, and the Max Planck Institute.

Peter von Bohlen studied at Halle, Bonn, Berlin, and Königsberg under Franz Bopp, Georg Wilhelm Freytag, and August Wilhelm von Schlegel. He later served as a professor of oriental literature at the University of Königsberg from 1825.

Peter von Bradke was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tartu, Tübingen, Jena, Leipzig, and Giessen, under scholars including Rudolf von Roth and Leo Meyer. He served as an associate professor at the University of Giessen from 1886 to 1896.

Petra Kieffer-Pülz is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Heinz Bechert between circa 1980 and 1991. She served as a Research Fellow at the Academy of Sciences and Literature, Mainz (attested 2013, 2016).

Petra Maurer is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who studied under Dieter Schuh and Dunchu Sonam Dorje. She has held posts at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, and the University of Munich.

Phakchok Rinpoche is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned a Khenpo title at Dzongsar Institute (~1997–2004) and studied under multiple traditional teachers. In circa 2004, he became Vajra Master at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling.
Pham Thi Tuyet Tam is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

Phanit Jetjiravat is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the academic advisement of Phra Suthithammanuwat, Veerachart Nimanong, and Paetpong Worapongpichet.
